summary: Iteration 3 tested Rain Alerts/watches, push endpoints, season plans, cron tick, payout celebration/simulate, Kalshi sync, the 5-tab mobile bar, and the landing research/pricing sections. Backend: 51/51 pytest pass when run serially with -n 0 (21 new tests in test_raincheck_iter3_features.py plus 30 regression tests). Checked: watch CRUD, 404/422 validation, and price-drop logic using baselines edited in Mongo (no change and small drop -> no alert; >=20% drop -> 'cheaper' alert fires once and the baseline resets; target hit -> fires; odds shift of 10+ points -> 'forecast' alert). Also: alerts read -> unread 0; push public-key, subscribe/unsubscribe and test (400 with no subs, 200 with a fake sub); plan preview, create and cancel, including budget and per-leg caps, legs matched to positions, 422/404 validation, and 400 in kalshi mode without creds; cron 200 returned in under 5s, 401 for a bad or missing token, duplicate:true for a repeated X-Webhook-Id; simulate hit/miss, 400 on a second simulate and on kalshi positions, 404 cross-user, celebrated flag, payout alert; kalshi/sync -> {synced:0}. Frontend (desktop 1920 and iPhone 390x844): all requested flows passed. The unread badge clears on /alerts; check-now shows a toast; the watch button creates a watch that appears under Watching and can be removed; the builder opens from both the report and /plans, the preview updates with weekends/budget, the kalshi chip shows a toast without creds, approve is disabled with no risks, approve creates a plan card, and cancel works; simulate-hit shows the celebration ($50, confetti canvas) and it doesn't show again after reload; simulate-miss shows 'Expired (sim)'; the sync button is hidden with no Kalshi positions; 5 tabs and Add a business are visible on mobile; PushToggle shows on /alerts and /settings; research has 3 sourced links and pricing renders. No blocking bugs. There are some logic and UX issues listed below.

minor.issue: 'Most it could pay' (max_payout) overstates coverage. Legs that aren't available yet use uncapped contracts (loss_if_event*coverage) and ignore the per-leg budget. Example: a $20 budget with 4 weekends showed $4,512, while run_plan would place only about 250 contracts per leg. Also, when per_leg < price, the preview forces contracts=max(1,...), and now_cost=min(est,budget) hides the overspend. run_plan would mark those legs over_budget instead, so preview and execution disagree.

Alert spam once the target is reached. After price <= target_price, every later 1c drop fires another 'cheaper' alert, because the baseline resets but the target stays. This happened in the live data: '26c down from 35c', then '24c down from 26c' from a cron tick. Suggest clearing target_price after the first target alert, or requiring the 20% rule after that.

There is no dedupe across plans. Two active plans for the same business both bought the same Cool Sat Oct 24 / Sun Oct 25 legs, so the user double-hedges. Consider warning about or blocking an overlapping active plan.
Deleting a paper position placed by a plan leaves the plan leg as 'Placed' with a dangling position_id and doesn't reduce plan.spent.
Dedupe is find_one then insert, with no unique index on cron_runs.run_id, so concurrent retries can race. Add a unique index and catch DuplicateKeyError.

The update isn't conditioned on status='open'. A concurrent simulate and refresh_positions could settle twice and create duplicate payout alerts and pushes. Use update_one({id, status:'open'}) and check modified_count.
celebrated returns ok for unknown ids (no 404). The business_id on a watch isn't checked for ownership.

issues: The 2 pricing cards sit in a 3-column grid and leave the right third empty on desktop. The cards also have no CTA buttons.
The StatusPill 'Paid $700 (sim)' wraps onto 2 lines inside md:w-24.
The text says to add RainCheck to the Home Screen first, but 'Turn on alerts' is still an enabled primary button. Consider hiding it or swapping in an install CTA.
The top-right toast briefly renders under the sticky header (header z-50). This carries over from iteration 2.

action_items: Cap preview contracts for unavailable legs by per_leg/est price (or show the payout range only for available legs), and make the preview match run_plan's over_budget behaviour
Stop repeat 'cheaper' alerts after target_price is reached (clear the target or require the 20% rule after the first fire)
Optional: dedupe or warn on overlapping active plans; reconcile the plan leg when a plan position is deleted
Optional: make settle() idempotent (filter on status open); add a unique index on cron_runs.run_id
Optional polish: pricing grid layout, wrapping of the Paid pill, PushToggle state on iOS when not installed
critical_code_review_comments: plan_preview returns max_payout = sum of contracts across all legs, ignoring budget for legs not yet listed, which misleads the user
check_watches: the target_price condition re-fires on every small drop once below target
settle() has no status guard (race leads to double payout alert/push)
cron_runs dedupe has no unique index
refresh_positions makes one Kalshi call per open position on every GET /positions and /dashboard, which will get slow as positions grow
seed_data_creation: Test data was cleaned up: my UI-created plan (cancelled) and its 2 positions, TEST_celebrate positions and their payout alert, TEST_ watches/alerts/push subs for test-user-2, and TEST_ cron run ids. test-user-1 still has its original active plan ba0a412c08f8 and watch b56a953ce623.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest with -n 0. pytest.ini enables xdist with loadscope, and the iter3 tests share test-user-2 state (watches/alerts), so parallel runs cause false failures. The iter3 tests edit Mongo directly (pymongo using MONGO_URL/DB_NAME from backend/.env) to force price-drop and forecast alerts for test-user-2. Calling cron/tick runs check_watches/run_plans for all users and can create real alerts for test-user-1. Never log out with test_session_raincheck.
